_mechanisms_active: face_says_stranger gate — a visible-but-unmatched face BLOCKS colour/re-ID from even attempting a match for that box
face_veto — a contradicting face rejects a colour/re-ID candidate match outright
Face-based registration gate (see _registration_note — unaffected by this flag, always on)
_mechanisms_disabled: ByteTrack ID-switch guard — if a track's code is already cached (from a PRIOR cycle, before this cycle's face-anchor logic runs), an occlusion hand-off to a different person is not detected; the wrong cached code is trusted
evidence gating — every sighting with a non-'Detecting...' code is logged unconditionally, including ones from a track mid-hand-off
_registration_note: Same as every other config: minting a new SDT code always requires a visible face (query_face_emb is not None), independent of enable_face_anchor. This flag only changes what happens to boxes that DON'T get a fresh face match — whether colour/re-ID may claim them for an existing person.
_expected_risk: Isolates face-anchoring's own contribution. Should prevent the specific 'colour matched a stranger to an existing code' failure mode from A, but is still exposed to ID-switch (cache never re-verified once set) and to unconfirmed evidence (a wrongly-cached code still gets photo evidence filed under it).
_tiling_note: DETECTION ONLY — identity flags identical to the untiled variant. min_source_resolution lowered to 640 for the 800x600 ChokePoint frames.
